May 12, 2020
Helping Local Families
Emily Fawcett
May 12, 2020
All Saints' Church has been called upon by the county to provide food for families in need who contact the PWC Food Line. We will be packing food from our pantry for these families in need beginning Monday, May 11.
Ways you can help! Sign up at
https://www.pwfoodrescue.org/
to pick up and deliver food for families in need in our community.
Thank you All Saints’ family, for finding creative ways to use your gifts to bless those in need!

As we make plans to climb aboard for mountains of fun at Rocky Railway VBS and since we cannot gather at the church for decorating parties, we want to extend an invitation for families and individuals to use your time at home for a great ministry project. We have 12 projects that can be done at home to begin preparing for this big adventure. here
and

heading_structure: h1: Rocky Railway VBS - Coming this Summer!
body_text:
Emily Fawcett
May 1, 2020
Rocky Railway VBS - Coming this Summer!
Emily Fawcett
May 1, 2020
Our Vacation Bible School theme this year is just the ticket in all of our lives as we adjust to new schedules, changes, trials, and transitions. In anticipation that the church will re-open again at least sometime this summer, we are preparing for a faith-filled adventure where kids discover that Jesus's power pulls us through! After prayerful planning, we believe a July or August, on-site VBS is the best approach this year, and plans are in the works to make it an event to remember! Children and their friends will track through Bible Adventures, explore science and crafts at Imagination Station, worship at Sing & Play Express, experience other energetic Railroad stations, and of course romp in the church backyard in Locomotion Games. More details coming soon!
Click here to watch the video

Apart Together Update as of Friday, May 8
Stay in Touch Online!
Missing your weekly fellowship? At All Saints’ Church your ministry leaders are working behind the scenes to bring back as many opportunities to “e-gather” and stay in the Word together. Right now you can attend “Zoom” meetings with the Tuesday and Thursday morning Women’s Bible Studies. Very soon we will also be bringing the Men’s Saturday Morning Bible Study back online, as well as enable some of the other small groups (who aren’t already) to continue to meet. Plus, we now have a
WEEKLY BIBLE QUIZ
available to test your knowledge. Visit our
Adult Resources Page
for information on the offerings below and more.
Thursdays:
Peacemaking Women | Tuesdays: Time with the Archbishop | Weekly Bible Quiz
Mark Your Calendars
We have a new Walk for Life Date! June 27 help us make a difference for LIFE!
The struggle for life has never been more grievous in our nation and our state. Stand for life when you
lead a team, join a team
or
support a team
in the
2020 Walk for Life
. The first ever joint Walk supports Care Net PRCs and
two
other life affirming local ministries in our community. Help us as we team up to save lives, support adoption, provide affordable healthcare to moms and babies and proclaim the Gospel. Our walkers include Cheryl Bull, Suzy Speare and Sandi Clark. Contact us to add your support, join our team or lead your own team! (Questions? Contact Sandi at 7038958493)
Learn more and register @

Acts 10:34-43 (ESV)
34
So Peter opened his mouth and said: “Truly I understand that God shows no partiality,
35
but in every nation anyone who fears him and does what is right is acceptable to him.
36
As for the word that he sent to Israel, preaching good news of peace through Jesus Christ (he is Lord of all),
37
you yourselves know what happened throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee after the baptism that John proclaimed:
38
how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power. He went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, for God was with him.
39
And we are witnesses of all that he did both in the country of the Jews and in Jerusalem. They put him to death by hanging him on a tree,
40
but God raised him on the third day and made him to appear,
41
not to all the people but to us who had been chosen by God as witnesses, who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead.
42
And he commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that he is the one appointed by God to be judge of the living and the dead.
43
To him all the prophets bear witness that everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name.”

Acts 8:26-38 (ESV)
26
Now an angel of the Lord said to Philip, “Rise and go toward the south to the road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza.” This is a desert place.
27
And he rose and went. And there was an Ethiopian, a eunuch, a court official of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was in charge of all her treasure. He had come to Jerusalem to worship
28
and was returning, seated in his chariot, and he was reading the prophet Isaiah.
29
And the Spirit said to Philip, “Go over and join this chariot.”
30
So Philip ran to him and heard him reading Isaiah the prophet and asked, “Do you understand what you are reading?”
31
And he said, “How can I, unless someone guides me?” And he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.
32
Now the passage of the Scripture that he was reading was this:
“Like a sheep he was led to the slaughter
and like a lamb before its shearer is silent,
so he opens not his mouth.
33
In his humiliation justice was denied him.
Who can describe his generation?
For his life is taken away from the earth.”
34
And the eunuch said to Philip, “About whom, I ask you, does the prophet say this, about himself or about someone else?”
35
Then Philip opened his mouth, and beginning with this Scripture he told him the good news about Jesus.
36
And as they were going along the road they came to some water, and the eunuch said, “See, here is water! What prevents me from being baptized?”
38
And he commanded the chariot to stop, and they both went down into the water, Philip and the eunuch, and he baptized him.

Acts 14:8-15 (ESV)
8
Now at Lystra there was a man sitting who could not use his feet. He was crippled from birth and had never walked.
9
He listened to Paul speaking. And Paul, looking intently at him and seeing that he had faith to be made well,
10
said in a loud voice, “Stand upright on your feet.” And he sprang up and began walking.
11
And when the crowds saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices, saying in Lycaonian, “The gods have come down to us in the likeness of men!”
12
Barnabas they called Zeus, and Paul, Hermes, because he was the chief speaker.
13
And the priest of Zeus, whose temple was at the entrance to the city, brought oxen and garlands to the gates and wanted to offer sacrifice with the crowds.

But when the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard of it, they tore their garments and rushed out into the crowd, crying out,
15
“Men, why are you doing these things? We also are men, of like nature with you, and we bring you good news, that you should turn from these vain things to a living God, who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all that is in them.

Acts 13:44-52 (ESV)
44
The next Sabbath almost the whole city gathered to hear the word of the Lord.
45
But when the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy and began to contradict what was spoken by Paul, reviling him.
46
And Paul and Barnabas spoke out boldly, saying, “It was necessary that the word of God be spoken first to you. Since you thrust it aside and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold, we are turning to the Gentiles.
47
For so the Lord has commanded us, saying,
“‘I have made you a light for the Gentiles,
that you may bring salvation to the ends of the earth.’”
48
And when the Gentiles heard this, they began rejoicing and glorifying the word of the Lord, and as many as were appointed to eternal life believed.
49
And the word of the Lord was spreading throughout the whole region.
50
But the Jews incited the devout women of high standing and the leading men of the city, stirred up persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and drove them out of their district.
51
But they shook off the dust from their feet against them and went to Iconium.
52
And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.

At that time the Feast of Dedication took place at Jerusalem. It was winter,

John 21:1-14 (ESV)
1
After this Jesus revealed himself again to the disciples by the Sea of Tiberias, and he revealed himself in this way.
2
Simon Peter, Thomas (called the Twin), Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, the sons of Zebedee, and two others of his disciples were together.
3
Simon Peter said to them, “I am going fishing.” They said to him, “We will go with you.” They went out and got into the boat, but that night they caught nothing.
4
Just as day was breaking, Jesus stood on the shore; yet the disciples did not know that it was Jesus.
5
Jesus said to them, “Children, do you have any fish?” They answered him, “No.”
6
He said to them, “Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some.” So they cast it, and now they were not able to haul it in, because of the quantity of fish.
7
That disciple whom Jesus loved therefore said to Peter, “It is the Lord!” When Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he put on his outer garment, for he was stripped for work, and threw himself into the sea.
8
The other disciples came in the boat, dragging the net full of fish, for they were not far from the land, but about a hundred yards off.
9
When they got out on land, they saw a charcoal fire in place, with fish laid out on it, and bread.
10
Jesus said to them, “Bring some of the fish that you have just caught.”
11
So Simon Peter went aboard and hauled the net ashore, full of large fish,
153
of them. And although there were so many, the net was not torn.
12
Jesus said to them, “Come and have breakfast.” Now none of the disciples dared ask him, “Who are you?” They knew it was the Lord.
13
Jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them, and so with the fish.
14
This was now the third time that Jesus was revealed to the disciples after he was raised from the dead.

Communications All Saints'
September 30, 2026
“Cheap grace is the deadly enemy of our Church. We are fighting to-day for costly grace.”
“When Christ calls a man, he bids him come and die.”
Considered a classic, Dietrich Bonhoeffer’s
The Cost of Discipleship
wrestles with the question of what it means to actually live the faith we proclaim as Christians.
In Bonhoeffer’s case, it meant execution at the hands of the Nazi regime during World War II.
The Cost of Discipleship
is available for purchase from the All Saints’ Bookshelf, located in the Atrium, for $14. Payment can be made by cash or check, or by credit card via an online form. See the Bookshelf for details.

page_title: A Pastoral Letter from Bishop Chris Warner
heading_structure: h1: A Pastoral Letter from Bishop Chris Warner
body_text:
Communications All Saints'
September 24, 2026
A Pastoral Letter from Bishop Chris Warner
Communications All Saints'
September 24, 2026
This letter is also available as a .pdf file
here
.
September 23, 2026
Dear Sisters and Brothers in Christ,
I write to you about an issue that touches something fundamental to our Christian faith:
the sacredness of every human life and our calling to protect those who are vulnerable especially the unborn
.
Our Christian conviction concerning the sanctity of life begins with our Sovereign Creator. Every human being is created in the image and likeness of God (Genesis 1:26–27), and therefore possesses a dignity that is not bestowed by the state, determined by usefulness, or dependent upon age, ability, health, independence, or circumstance.
Our own Anglican Church in North America speaks clearly about this. The Canons affirm that “God, and not man, is the creator of human life. The unjustified taking of life is sinful. Therefore, all members and clergy are called to promote and respect the sanctity of every human life from conception to natural death.” (Title II, Canon 8, Section 3)
This is part of what Pope John Paul II memorably called “the Gospel of life.” In the encyclical Evangelium Vitae, he wrote that the Gospel of life stands at the very heart of the message of Jesus and must be proclaimed as good news to every generation and culture.
That Gospel of life is broad and reflective of the goodness of God. We must remember that it is much larger than a single political issue.
John Paul II reminds us that threats to human life include not only abortion and euthanasia, but also poverty, hunger, war, the arms trade, drugs, environmental destruction, and other circumstances that assault human dignity and destroy human life. Christians cannot selectively defend human dignity. We are called to protect the unborn child, care for the mother in crisis, defend children from exploitation, stand with the poor, welcome the stranger, oppose human

Al Qaeda-affiliated militants (terrorists) in Mali recently increased the amount of territory they hold. body_text:
Communications All Saints'
September 16, 2026
Food Giveaway: Prayers for Health and Family
Communications All Saints'
September 16, 2026
Food Giveaway prayer report
We had a good turnout of people on September 12 who came in for prayer. Including a couple of people from All Saints', we totaled 27 overall. Some of the others who came in for prayer were families with four or five people together, including little kids.
We gave out at least five prayer shawls and four Bibles (two Hispanic and two English).
A couple things to note:
Mother Valarie prayed for a woman who wanted prayer for her hurting knee. There was a little bit of a language barrier, but Valarie knew enough Spanish to not only pray for her, but also to understand what she said. The woman went from saying her knee felt good to it felt better to finally excellent, meaning there was no more pain.
Others requested prayers for health and family.
We had a mother and son come in. The son is 24 and was leaving the next week for Army boot camp in North Carolina. They wanted prayers for safety and protection. After he received prayer, the man said he felt better.
A big thanks to Father Patricio for his help in translating for two groups that came in for prayer. It made things so much easier.

Would you pray about partnering with us? You can participate in three different ways.

Communications All Saints'

Adults
Why "Formation"?
Communications All Saints'
September 9, 2026
Adults
by Mother Maryanna Stumbaugh
You may have noticed that Adult Education (or Adult Discipleship) is now being referred to as Adult
Formation
.
This may seem innocuous, but it is actually an exciting shift we are making intentionally and in prayerful discernment.
The word “formation” expresses more of a holistic approach, as we seek to be transformed by the power of the Holy Spirit into the image of God. We are called to love the Lord our God not only with our minds but with our whole heart and strength. “Formation” describes this focus — not only intellectual edification, but to include the formation of our beings conforming to Christ.
We intentionally engage this work as one body, one community in Christ. So we invite you to invest in the Adult Formation hour on Sunday mornings from 9:45 a.m. to 10:45 a.m.!

Communications All Saints'
August 26, 2026
formation
,
event
Kick-Off Sunday is September 13!
Communications All Saints'
August 26, 2026
formation
,
event
KICK-OFF SUNDAY, SEPTEMBER 13
8:15 a.m. & 11 a.m. — Prayers for students and the school year at both services
9:45 a.m. — New Christian Formation classes for all ages
4 p.m. — Kick-Off Picnic with slip’n slide & games
(bring your own picnic dinner & lawn chairs)
6 p.m. —
Matthew Clark
in concert
Come check out all the season has to offer!
You’ll find new Christian Formation classes for children, youth, and adults, including
God’s Big Story
children’s Sunday School, PreK and Kindergarten classes, a class for Grades 1-3, a new Grade 4/5 class, and a continuation of
GO!
Upper & Lower Children’s Church!
Stop by the Fall Sign-Up Table to register your child for the 2026-2027 Children’s Ministry school year.
Registering your child updates your personal info and helps us know how to prepare for our growing Sunday School classes and Children’s Church numbers.
Stop by the table for donut holes, fun tattoos for the kids, and check out our new FALL plans!
SMILE! Our Children’s Fall Kick-Off includes Picture Day!
Children are invited to have their photos updated (or taken for the first time) for their own personal cubby in the Children’s Wing hallway.
Nursery age and up.
BACKPACK BLESSINGS!
Students will be invited to come forward during the announcements at both services, with their school backpacks, as we pray for them and the school year.
Our
new Adult Formation offering
begins September 13.
Brand new Christian Formation classes for
Middle School
and High School students start September 13
in the Multi-Purpose Room.
KICK-OFF PICNIC &
MATTHEW CLARK
IN CONCERT!
Bring your own picnic dinner and lawn chairs. We’ll enjoy the slip’n slide and lawn games beginning at 4 p.m.  The concert begins at 6 p.m. Come for part or stay and enjoy the whole evening!

men

Men's Prayer Breakfast May 16
Communications All Saints'
April 29, 2026
men
,
prayer
All men of All Saints’ and their guests are invited to breakfast at All Saints’ Church at 7:30 a.m. on May 16.
We’ll enjoy a time of food, fellowship, prayer, teaching, and ministry updates.
Please contact Jim Morrison at 571.338.5774 by text or voice to help ensure a good amount of food is available.
Taste and see that the Lord is good; blessed is the one who takes refuge in him.
Psalm 34:8

Easter Memorial Flowers - Donations Open Now!
Guest User
March 22, 2021
church
,
community

holy week
Are you looking to memorialize a loved on or celebrate a special thanksgiving during this Easter season?
You can now honor your loved ones, past or present, with a special gift of beauty by making a donation for Easter lilies!
All Easter memorials and thanksgivings will be projected on Easter morning and will be included on the website, social media, and newsletter.
If interested, please fill out the form below. Donations will be accepted via check to the church office or through our PayPal link.
Sign-Up Here

The Art of Parenting: Aiming Your Child’s Heart Toward God
The years are short, but the days are long. All parents need encouragement along the way. Experience Adult Sunday School with
FAMILY LIFE'S Art of Parenting!
This 8-session, video-based study is designed to not only encourage and find new ways to integrate faith into everyday parenting moments, but also to create an environment where moms and dads can shoulder burdens together, celebrate breakthroughs, and relate to one another’s day-to-day parenting journey. Parents of all ages & stages invited!
Inspired by Psalm 127:4, the teaching sessions and conversations will cover the following topics:
The Goal of Parenting
Forming Character
Applying Discipline
Building Relationships
Understanding Identity
Nurturing Identity
Preparing for Mission
The Power of Family
How to Join In!
Attend
"Pastries for Parents" Coffee Hour Meet-n-Greet

Class runs 8 weeks, September 18- early November.

body_text:

Sunday Evenings- Foundations for Ministry- Year 1
Guest User
August 10, 2021
WHAT IS FOUNDATIONS FOR MINISTRY
?
An adult Bible study course designed for those willing to make a commitment to daily Bible study.
Intended for those who wish to deepen their understanding of Scripture and our Christian heritage.
It will also equip you to meet the challenges of ministry in the Church and in the world.
Course Format
It is a two-year course of Bible study.  It is divided into two academic years.
Year 1: Old Testament (Beginning September 10, 2023)
Year 2: New Testament (Fall 2024)*
Participants commit to one year of study at a time.
* Participants must complete Year 1 to be eligible to enroll in Year 2.
Weekly Meetings and Small Groups
Each week there will be a short teaching session and small group discussion.
Discussions are based on the weekly homework and include topics such as Bible study skills, personal application, scriptural content, theological concepts, and interpretation of Scripture.
The program requires a commitment to daily study, homework, class attendance, and a willingness to share within a small group.
Foundations groups form a close-knit environment for participants to share what they are learning, and grow in their knowledge of Scripture and their relationship with the Lord and one another.
Beginning on September 10, the class will meet on Sunday evenings from 4-6 p.m. The class will meet at the church from September to June, breaking for 3 weeks at Christmas, 1 week at Easter and 1 week at Memorial Day.
Course Materials
A participant’s workbook ($40/participant/year and only available from All Saints’)
An approved study bible (study notes and tools in these versions are used as part of the study):**
ESV Study Bible

The bride of Jesus Christ in our generation is nearly paralyzed by unbelief. God is calling His bride to a fresh and lavish anointing of faith. This study examines the lives of Abraham, Moses, and others as examples of persons who believed God. In this 10-week Beth Moore Bible Study, participants will explore this vital topic. Hi, Youth Families!
I'm excited to share our plans for Sunday nights as we enter 2021. As we are still right in the middle of the COVID pandemic, it has been a challenging season to plan, prepare, and express ministry in a way that feels normal and worthwhile. There are so many factors to consider and account for in ways that those in ministry haven't had to think about before. The good news is that we are not left to our own, God is with us and he is faithful to help his pastors guide his people.
Beginning Jan. 24 we will dig into a study series titled Can I Ask That? from Fuller Youth Institute. It's part of a program Fuller calls Sticky Faith (a faith in God that lasts). From Fuller Youth Institute: "A recent survey asked leaders of campus-based atheist clubs why they don't believe in God. Their responses were revealing: many had actually been involved in youth ministry during their high school years, and they named the church's failure to engage difficult questions as a key reason they left. Specifically, these young people cited the church's failure to wrestle with issues like the reliability of the biblical text, evolution vs. creation, and the exclusivity of Jesus. These students did not say they left their faith because of the stance their church took on the issues above. They left because the church failed to address them at all. When tough questions were addressed, the answers were found to be vague and superficial."
We are not looking to be vague or superficial here at All Saints' Youth. We want to engage issues and topics that you are struggling with, knowing that in that struggle and tension God is with us the whole time and will increase and strengthen our faith. It doesn't mean that we will solve every problem we encounter or have all of the answers to every question raised. It does mean that we will b

Please come twice a month on Tuesday evenings, beginning September 22, by Zoom (and on occasion at Panera for a parents night out!!) from 7-8 p.m. for discussion of a beloved bestseller,
Liturgy of the Ordinary: Sacred Practices of Everyday Life
by Tish Harrison Warren. In the overlooked moments and routines of our day, we can become aware of God's presence in surprising ways. How do we embrace the sacred in the ordinary and the ordinary in the sacred? Framed around one ordinary day, this book explores daily life through the lens of liturgy, small practices, and habits that form us. Each chapter looks at something―making the bed, brushing her teeth, losing her keys―that the author does every day. Drawing from the diversity of her life as a campus minister, Anglican priest, friend, wife, and mother, Tish Harrison Warren opens up a practical theology of the everyday. Each activity is related to a spiritual practice as well as an aspect of our Sunday worship. Come and discover the holiness of your every day.
Use the button below to send Tara an email if you’d like the Zoom link and more details.

Anglican Doma

Adults
CLASS IS FULL - Registration is closed
We will be doing an introductory session on Wednesday, September 16 at 7 p.m. for those who would like to explore this topic or ask questions before starting the full course.
Covid19 has turned our world upside down; we now talk of our “new normal.” There has been a lot of reports on the number of deaths as a result of this pandemic.  As much as most of us would rather not think about it, aging and dying are not only normal but universal. Not only will all of us die one day, but many of us will care for parents, family, and friends going through the aging and dying process. All Saints’ will be offering a course this fall on aging and dying.
Embrace the Journey is an 8-week adult education series designed to help you and your church understand and apply God’s Word to end of life issues.  Topics include the biblical view of life, preparing for the golden years, advance directives and advanced care plans, health care, hastening death, funeral plans and the role of the church in suffering and grief. Other sections can be added as needed. Each week’s session has a short video followed by group discussion. Registration is required; please register using the button below, so we can send you class information and have a Participant Guide ready for you. Each Participant Guide is $20 and includes the Finishing Life: Preparing for the End of Life booklet and full scripts from the video teaching. Couples can purchase an extra copy of Finishing Life for $5 each. This course will meet via Zoom on Wednesday evenings from 7-9 p.m. beginning September 23. If you have further questions please call or email Desiree Barker at the church office 703-670-0093 or at
dbarker@allsaintswoodbridge.org

Mission Desafio Inc. (the Rev. Dana & Damaris Craft)

Cristo Mi Redentor (Christ my Redeemer) in Guatemala City was planted within the heart of the community, a respite for those who work within the giant chasm that the city uses for waste disposal. The ministry was given a parcel of land on which to construct the first ACNA Church in Guatemala. The building serves a dual purpose, that of a Chapel and as a Community Center providing classes and daycare for all those dwelling in Nuevo Amanecer. The Gospel is delivered right in the center of their community.

body_text:
Anglican Doma
October 22, 2020
Common Recovery
Anglican Doma
October 22, 2020
At
Common Recovery
our goal is to
shower Prince William County with a message of hope; cultivating a community of recovery through recovery services, spiritual growth and peer housing. Evangelizing the working poor and raising up effective leaders from the least, the last and the lost.
This  program is known for its message of recovery for those who are hopelessly struggling with alcohol/drug addiction and have found no other way out.
It is our desire to reach out to those who are still suffering and lost.
We are here to pass on what was freely given to us —
“a message of hope.”
We were once on a path of destruction ourselves – addicted to alcohol and drugs. Alone in that dark pit of misery; we were desperate for change; but not able to stop! Our hearts cry was that God would stop the madness! That He would deliver us from that lifestyle that only promised death.
As recovered addicts ourselves, we understand & can help. It’s about staying clean & sober but that’s not all there’s more– it’s about getting our lives back as well!
Download a brochure here.

body_text:
Anglican Doma
October 19, 2020
StreetLight Community Outreach Ministries
Anglican Doma
October 19, 2020
After handing one woman a check for her overdue rent, she broke down in tears of relief. Between sobs, she told us for months she had been overcome with anxiety about where her children would sleep if they were evicted from their apartment. She had worked as a maid for a family that was forced to lay her off during the pandemic, which left her with no income and ineligible for unemployment. Sadly, her story is not uncommon. The National Low Income Housing Coalition recently announced 30-40 million Americans would face eviction by the end of the year - a direct result of the economic slowdown and massive job losses caused by the coronavirus outbreak .

Missionary Support: Global Mobilization Ministries (the Rev. Canon Dr. Alison Barfoot)

The Rev. Canon Alison L. Barfoot serves as the Assistant for International Relations to the Archbishop of Uganda. This ministry represents the cutting edge of mission strategy in the church today, for Uganda is not only a mission field—it is also an incredibly ripe mission force with which we can partner to fulfill the Great Commission (Matt. 28:16-20). LENT 2024: TRUE FASTING
from ACNA’s Matthew 25 Initiative
At the Matthew 25 Initiative, our desire is to see the unseen and the marginalized treasured.
And this Lenten season, we will be telling the stories of the least of these through 40 days of Anglican-informed, inspiring, beautiful, and theologically robust engagement pieces — in the vein of the church's traditional disciplines of Lent:  prayer, fasting, and almsgiving.
For our third year of Lent, we once again invite you to join us on a journey of normalizing Anglican justice and mercy by thoughtfully engaging in this historic Christian season of prayer, fasting, and almsgiving – this time, through the lens of Isaiah 58:6-12.

here

Stephen Minister
Guest User
September 13, 2022
There are times when every one of us experiences difficulties and could benefit from the care of a supportive Christian friend.
Our Stephen Ministers provide confidential, one-on-one Christian care to people who are:
• Grieving the death of a loved one
• Hospitalized or recovering from hospitalization
• Lonely or discouraged
• Coping with a terminal illness or caring for a family member with a terminal illness
• Unemployed or in a job crises
• Disabled or caring for an ill or disabled family member
• New to the congregation or the community
• Anticipating or recovering from the birth or adoption of a child
• Homebound or institutionalized
• Recently retired
• Experiencing a spiritual crisis
• Victim of a disaster or accident
• Or experiencing one of life’s other transitions
What is a Stephen Minister?
Stephen Ministers are members of our congregation who have received 50 hours of caregiving training to minister to people experiencing a crisis, facing a challenge, or simply going through a tough time. They are under the supervision of the congregation’s Stephen Leaders and Deacon Julie Tilton.
A Stephen Minister will meet with you privately and confidentially on a weekly basis to pray, listen, care, encourage, support, and remind you of Christ’s presence in your life.
(A Stephen Minister is not a counselor, nor a problem-solver, nor someone who runs errands or helps with chores.)
How do you get connected with a Stephen Minister?
Stephen Ministers are assigned to parishioners by Deacon Julie Tilton. Requests can be initiated by either the individual desiring a Stephen Minister, or by the Practical Care Coordinator coordinating a person’s care needs.
More information on Stephen Ministry can be found
online
, or by speaking with Deacon Julie Tilton.

Please notify the All Saints’ office or send an
email
if you are hospitalized and would like a trained parishioner or clergy member to visit you. If you contact Congregational Care Ministry, be sure to include the name of the hospital, the dates you anticipate being hospitalized, and a callback number.
Reconciliation of a Penitent:
Please contact a clergy member directly if you would like to be reconciled to God through the ministry of reconciliation.
From the Book of Common Prayer:
The reconciliation of a penitent is available for all who desire it. It is not restricted to times of sickness. Confessions may be heard anytime and anywhere.
The secrecy of a confession is morally absolute for the person hearing the confession and must under no circumstances be broken.
Funeral:
Please contact the All Saints’ office immediately upon the death of a parishioner or member of a parishioner’s family. Funeral arrangements should be made in consultation with a clergy member.

body_text:
Guest User
October 12, 2022
Story Time in the Park
Guest User
October 12, 2022
Story Time in the Park is a tangible way that All Saints’ Church is reaching the surrounding Dale City Community families.
Starting in 2020 with various locations, Story Time now takes place every Thursday at Cloverdale Park.
Our Children’s Ministry Director, Tara Pedersen, has formed relationships with the moms, dads, and children who come — parents often join in and participate as well. These relationships have led to families attending (and serving) in Vacation Bible School and participating in Sunday morning activities.
Story Time in the Park promotes literacy and the benefits of reading to children. It also provides snacks and an educational craft for all children who attend.

Bitter & Sweet: A Journey Into Easter
by Tsh Oxenreider
In a world that celebrates indulging our whims whenever we want, practicing the traditions of Lent is countercultural. When we welcome the temporary suffering of Lent, we swim upstream in a culture that goes with the flow.
The practice isn’t about proving our worth or earning God’s love; it’s about remembering how dependent we are on our Maker while we live here in our temporary, fragile bodies.

The new Zoom Homebound small group on Thursdays 7-8:30 p.m. will begin a new study September 7th on “Forever”, a video Bible study developed by Dr. Paul Tripp.
Instead of embracing the world's motto---'you only live once'---follow Tripp as he unpacks the biblical truth of the world as a broken place, longing for a second chance. And come alive as you discover the meaning and redemption all this brokenness can bring to your life today!
Dr. Tripp attended Columbia Bible College (now Columbia International University) and majored in Bible and Christian Education. He went on to receive his M.Div from the Reformed Episcopal Seminary and his D.Min in Biblical Counseling from Westminster Theological Seminary.
If you are homebound and want to join, all you need is a computer or a smart phone, and internet service. If you don’t know how to use Zoom, we can help you. Please contact Deacon Julie Tilton at jtilton@allsaintswoodbridge.org.

body_text:
You are invited to worship at All Saints’ Church during Holy Week 2026:
The last week of Lent, Holy Week, remembers the last week of Christ’s earthly life, beginning with Palm Sunday’s commemoration of Jesus’ triumphal entry into Jerusalem (Matt 21:1-11).
At All Saints’, you have the opportunity to worship each day during Holy Week. Nursery care is provided at many of these services (noted below). If you would like nursery care during the Easter Vigil on Saturday, please
RSVP
to Tara Pedersen.
March 29:
Palm Sunday Services
(Nursery available for age 5 and under, Sunday School & Children's Church)
March 30: Holy Eucharist, 12 p.m.
March 31: Holy Eucharist, 12 p.m.
April 1: Holy Eucharist, 6:30 a.m., 8 a.m., & 12 p.m.
April 2:
Maundy Thursday
, 7 p.m. (Nursery care provided)
April 3:
Good Friday
, 7 p.m. (Nursery care provided)
April 4:
Easter Vigil
(If you would like nursery care during the Easter Vigil on Saturday, please
RSVP
to Tara Pedersen.)
April 5:
Easter Sunday
(Nursery care provided, no Sunday School or Children’s Church)
Palm Sunday
Sunday, march 29, 8:15 & 11 a.m.
ChildCare provided; Sunday school for all ages at 9:45 a.m.
On Palm Sunday, we remember Jesus’ triumphal entry into Jerusalem (see
Matthew 21:1-11, Mark 11:1-11, Luke 19:28-44, and John 12:12-19
).
Services on Palm Sunday begin with “the Procession of the Palms,” where worshippers hold palm branches as they process into the church.
Sometimes Palm Sunday is also called/celebrated as “Passion Sunday,” a commemoration of Jesus’ suffering and death. However, Passion Sunday used to be celebrated on the Sunday
before
Palm Sunday, the fifth and last Sunday of Lent.
Here is the Collect for Palm Sunday:
Almighty and everliving God, in your tender love for the human race you sent your Son our Savior Jesus Christ to take upon himself our nature, and to suffer death upon the cross, giving us the example of his great humility: Mercifully grant that we may walk in the way of his suffering, and also share in h

body_text:
Sunday Morning Services:
8:15 a.m. & 11 a.m.
Almighty God, to you all hearts are open, all desires known, and from you no secrets are hid:
Cleanse the thoughts of our hearts by the inspiration of your Holy Spirit,
that we may perfectly love you, and worthily magnify your holy Name;
through Christ our Lord.
Amen.
The Collect for Purity,
Book of Common Prayer
(p. 123)
All are invited to worship with us in our Anglican tradition of Holy Eucharist each Sunday at 8:15 a.m. or 11 a.m. Our services generally last 90 minutes; nursery care and Children’s Church are available during both. We include a mix of contemporary music and hymns in our worship. Our prayers are found in the
Book of Common Prayer
(2019). Take a look at the order of service for Sundays
here.
You can expect to see a range of dress from casual to formal. Visitors are welcome to dress as they are most comfortable attending a Sunday morning service. However you choose to join us, you will be welcome!

What We Believe
All Saints’ Church is rooted in the historic interpretation of the Christian Bible—which is summarized in the words of the Apostles' and Nicene Creeds. Our specific theological convictions are expressed in the Thirty-Nine Articles of the Anglican Communion. All Saints' Church is part of the
Anglican Church in North America
and is under Bishop Chris Warner of the
Diocese of the Mid-Atlantic
.
Each Sunday we confess our faith in the words of the Nicene Creed.

Our Vestry
The Vestry currently consists of the Rector and nine elected lay members. Each elected lay member serves a three-year term. Children’s Ministry
“
...so that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith—that you, being rooted and grounded in love...
”
— Ephesians 3:17
The Children’s Ministry at All Saints’ Church serves infants, toddlers, and children through the fifth grade. While we recognize and affirm that the spiritual development of children is first and foremost a parent’s responsibility, our church is poised and ready to assist! We seek to partner with you and support your family in training up children to love and serve the Lord each day of their lives. Children are welcomed, valued, protected, and lovingly cared for while they learn who Jesus is, how to follow Him and how the truths of the Bible can help them to make Godly choices. Our dedicated Children’s Ministry team is committed to helping children:
Understand that God earnestly desires a personal, meaningful and growing relationship through Jesus with them
Read, know, and love God’s word
Learn how to engage in daily prayer and worship
Experience God’s presence through the Holy Spirit as an integral part of their lives
Voluntarily participate in acts of service
Become committed to using their spiritual gifts
Grow in Christ-like character

Prayer Ministry
“
Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God.
”
— Philippians 4:6
All Saints’ Church has been called by God to be a “House of Prayer.” We welcome your prayer requests regarding any and all concerns or praise reports for you, your family members or friends.
Prayer Requests
All prayer requests will be prayed for by the intercessory team for two weeks. Please be specific about your request (e.g. healing of cancer, etc.) and, if submitting for someone else, please note your relationship to this person, (e.g. yourself or your mother, son, uncle, cousin, neighbor, co-worker, etc.) Please note, we would love to receive a follow-up report, whether more prayer is needed or your prayers are answered. Contact Deacon Julie (
jtilton@allsaintswoodbridge.org
) with your feedback or submit a
praise report online
. We love to give God praise for answered prayer!
(Boxes with an asterisk must be filled in).
Other Ways to Receive Prayer
During the Prayers of the People, there will be a time for the congregation to participate aloud by lifting up personal names.

Safeguarding (formerly “Protecting God’s Children”)
All Saints’ Church takes seriously the protection of our youngest saints as well as vulnerable adults. We require extensive training for those individuals working with our children.
We have researched and established “Best Practices” to protect God’s children which include:
Careful screening of all staff and volunteers who work with children (applications, personal reference checks, national sexual offender registry and criminal background checks, etc.)
Interaction and Monitoring Guidelines (two-person rule at all times)
A Coded Check In-Check Out System with one entrance to the Children’s Wing
Please contact
Tara Pedersen
, Children’s Ministry Director, for more information on our safeguards or to register for one of our upcoming workshops. Childcare is available upon request.

body_text:
The Nursery
All Saints’ Church offers three unique nurseries for the children from birth through the age of four:
Infant
,
Wobbler
, and
Toddler
. Each space is thoughtfully equipped with developmentally appropriate toys and books, and lovingly staffed by paid employees and dedicated volunteers. The nurseries are located just down the hall from the Sanctuary inside the Children's Wing. Doors that allow the top to open separately connect the three nurseries; this helps us keep a steady flow of communication between our three different areas for little ones. We think you'll find each nursery just right for meeting the developmental needs of the children for which it was designed!
Nurseries are open on Sunday mornings for the 8:15 a.m. service, the Discipleship hour (9:45-10:45 a.m.) and for the 11 a.m. church service. The infant nursery is also open for large church events for which arrangements have been specifically made. For other events during the week infants may be dropped off for care in the toddler nursery.
Paid staff and volunteers are trained prior to working in the nurseries.  Occasionally, mature teens work alongside experienced infant nursery volunteers or staff.
If you have questions or would like more information, please contact Tara Pedersen (
tpedersen@allsaintswoodbridge.org
) or Asteir Shokai (
ashokai@allsaintswoodbridge.org
) at 703-670-0093.
Parents are welcome in any of our nurseries for the purposes of nursing, feeding, changing, or comforting their children at any time!
Registering Your Child in Our Nurseries
When first visiting All Saints' Church, you will be asked to register your children to let us know more about your children and how you would like us to care for them. Please visit the Welcome/Check-in center (booth just outside the children's wing entrance) to register your child or you can fill out the registration form.

body_text:
Sick Child Nursery Policy
While we welcome the opportunity to play with and pray with your child, we respectfully request that you do NOT bring your child to the nurseries when he or she:
has a fever (children must be fever-free for 24 hours without the use of fever-reducing medicine before being allowed into the nurseries)
has vomited in the past 12 hours
has had diarrhea in the past 12 hours
has nasal drainage that is not clear
is excessively coughing/hacking or sneezing
has an infection and has not been on an antibiotic for 24 hours
has a rash or skin infection
is lethargic and not feeling well, or seems to be coming down with something
You may be called on to pick up your child if the nursery staff feels your child is sick.  Thanks for helping us keep our youngest saints healthy!

body_text:
Upton Farm Family Cemetery
(located on All Saints’ Church property)
researched and written by Jay Rarick
All Saints’ Church property contains an abandoned cemetery that belonged to the Upton family who farmed this land in the 19th and early 20th centuries. An archaeological study commissioned by All Saints’ Church established there were at least five burials in the cemetery. The burials were marked with plain field stones of various descriptions rather than carved grave markers.
There were two families of Uptons in the Occoquan District of Prince William County in the 19th century. One includes a white family who eventually occupied the property along the historic alignment of Smoketown Road and another was a mulatto family who resided in the area closer to the town of Occoquan. There is no indication of any family connection between these two groups and the study focused on the white family who eventually bought the property on Smoketown Road.
The first generation of record begins before the 1840 census with a William Upton (hereinafter referred to as William "Sr.") who was a boatman and later a farmer.
According to county records, William H. Upton (William "Jr.") and his brother John T. Upton in 1870 and 1883 purchased the first of the land along Smoketown Road which would become the Upton farm.
The farm passed to William Jr. and his wife, Mary Jane Upton, and their children.
By 1880 there were William Jr. and his wife Mary Jane and their three remaining children, William H. (William III), Mary Catherine and John Thomas Upton, living on the farm. By 1890 William Jr. is paying real estate tax ($0.59) on 24 acres, which probably contained what is today the family cemetery. All of this family is shown living on the property in the 1900 census, but by 1910, William Jr. is no longer recorded in the census. body_text:
The Jerusalem Cross
Behind the altar is the Jerusalem cross that has hung in that same spot both here in our new building and in our former building on Saratoga Lane since that church was first built.
The Jerusalem Cross is a Christian symbol consisting of a large cross surrounded by four smaller crosses, one in each quadrant. Over the years, the Jerusalem cross has acquired a number of interpretations. The five crosses can symbolize the five wounds of Christ during the Passion; the Pentateuch (the first five books of the Bible); and, perhaps the first five Christian churches. The four smaller crosses are also said to be symbolic of the four Gospels proclaimed to the four corners of the earth, beginning in Jerusalem; the large cross in the center symbolizes the person of Christ.
This cross is a very special symbol for All Saints’ Church—it speaks to who we are. As Jesus told His disciples to go forth and proclaim the Gospel to all the world, we, too, are charged to spread the Good News of Christ in our own world, in Woodbridge, from Saratoga Lane and Gideon Drive. When we see the Jerusalem cross, we are reminded that our own church is not to be a self-contained entity, but to be welcoming and to serve, reaching out in boldness to our community.
We are called to “love and serve the Lord” and All Saints’ has been a church that “equips the Saints (us) for ministry.” Now we are to be a church “overflowing with God’s love and healing power.” Christ, symbolically the center of the Jerusalem cross, reminds us that He equips us, we are filled with the power of the Holy Spirit, and He wants us to use our gifts, our training, and His power to love, grow and serve in His name.

body_text:
Timeline
All Saints’ roots date back to the first Anglican church established in Prince William County in 1667 when a chapel was built on the banks of Quantico Creek in Dumfries.
January 1, 1980
St. Martin's, a mission church in the Dumfries-Quantico area started in 1955 by Trinity Episcopal in Manassas, and Holy Spirit, a mission church in Dale City started in 1963 by St. Margaret’s, merge to form All Saints’. The bishop proposed the merger since St. Martin’s had a building, but no priest, while Holy Spirit had a priest, but no building. Conditions of the merger included calling a new vicar and building a new church in Dale City. The Rev. Chuck Stein, who had been vicar of Holy Spirit, continued as interim vicar of the combined congregations until he retired on Dec. 31, 1980. Paula Woods and Robert Pritchard followed as interim vicars.
Feb. 17, 1980
All Saints’ holds its first service at the old St. Martin’s building in Triangle.
December 1981
The Rev. John A.M. Guernsey called as All Saints’ new vicar
March 3, 1983
All Saints’ holds its first service in its new building on Saratoga Lane in Dale City
April 10, 1983
All Saints’ is dedicated
AUGUST 1985
The Rev. Whis Hays and the Rev. Mary Hays join All Saints’ as associate vicars
SEPTEMBER 1987
Mary Hays leaves for Truro Church in Fairfax
Jan. 31, 1988
All Saints’ gains full parish status
JUNE 1989
The Rev. Valarie Whitcomb joins All Saints’ as associate rector
SEPTEMBER 1989
Whis Hayes leaves All Saints’ to start Rock the World Youth Mission Alliance in Ambridge, PA
1995
The original prayer room built as part of a six-room expansion
May 2001
All Saints’ purchases 28 acres of land on Gideon Drive in Woodbridge next to Hylton Chapel to build a new, larger church to hold the growing congregation
NOV. 2005
The Rev. Mark Brown joins All Saints’ as associate rector
Dec. 10, 2006
Congregation votes to leave The Episcopal Church, becoming part of the Anglican Diocese of North Kigezi within the Church of Uganda
Sept. 2007
J

Featured
The Road to Resurrection
The Road to Resurrection began in 2021 as an outreach to the community during Holy Week, leading up to Easter. Similar to The Living Nativity, there are costumed scenes from the Bible. Participants get to walk around the property to experience each scene leading up to the death and resurrection of Jesus. This family friendly event has live animals, a petting zoo, crafts, trikes, an Easter egg hunt, and door prizes!
Read more →
Food Giveaways
Food Giveaways have been a monthly occurrence at All Saints’ Church since March of 2021. What makes the Food Giveaways unique to those who come through is the variety of fresh produce, meat, bread, and milk. Additionally guests of the Food Giveaways can choose from the nonperishable or canned goods, ensuring they get the food that best suits their families needs. The Food Giveaways offer a prayer tent for anyone in need of specific prayer.
Read more →
Vacation Bible School
After a Virtual VBS in 2020, Vacation Bible School has been on location at All Saints’ Church since 2021! VBS is open to all children in the community, and special invitations were made to those attending our monthly Food Giveaways, and Story Time at the Park. The format of Vacation Bible School at All Saints’ Church allows children to be in small groups (called crews) that they travel around the building with all week! Bible points for each day make the Gospel message easy to understand for children who don’t attend a local church. VBS volunteers serve in all different areas throughout the week, and members of the community are welcomed into our beautiful building.

body_text:
Employment Opportunities
Working at All Saints’ Church provides the opportunity to serve God and His people in a thriving, multi-generational, and diverse congregation in Northern Virginia. We are a church within the
Anglican Church in North America
nationally and the
Diocese of the Mid-Atlantic
locally.
music director
Full-time, 40 hours per week, with health benefits
All Saints’ Church is seeking a full-time Music Director to provide leadership in all areas of musical worship in the life of our vibrant and growing congregation. Prospective candidates will model a mature personal faith in Jesus Christ, excel in leading blended musical worship which incorporates traditional hymnody with contemporary Christian worship in a distinctly Anglican context, and further develop and integrate music and worship arts into all areas of congregational life. This position has an important role in the Sunday morning worship services, as All Saints’ Church seeks to bring the diverse members of our community into the presence of God. The Music Director reports directly to the Rector.
This role is not open to musicians who are only seeking “gig” work but instead we are seeking someone who desires to invest in this community. Every member of the All Saints’ staff team works together to build community together and as such this full-time ministry position must take priority over other work or performance opportunities.
Essential Ministry Roles and Responsibilities
Leads and/or oversees all aspects of Music Ministry in consultation with the Rector
Plans and leads musical worship for all Sunday services, special services, and events throughout the year in accordance with the ACNA liturgical calendar year
Directs Sunday musical teams (instrumentalists and vocalists) helping current team members to continue to develop musically and spiritually and actively recruits and develops new team members
Leads worship teams and choir rehearsal one night each week
Prepares communications and ministry

“...so that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith—that you, being rooted and grounded in love...

The Children’s Ministry at All Saints’ Church serves infants, toddlers, and children through the fifth grade. While we recognize and affirm that the spiritual development of children is first and foremost a parent’s responsibility, our church is poised and ready to assist! Children are welcomed, valued, protected, and lovingly cared for while they learn who Jesus is, how to follow Him and how the truths of the Bible can help them to make Godly choices. Our dedicated Children’s Ministry team is committed to helping children:
Understand that God earnestly desires a personal, meaningful and growing relationship through Jesus with them

Learn how to engage in daily prayer and worship

Baptism
This public declaration of faith in Jesus Christ takes place during Sunday morning worship on or near five occasions each year: Pentecost, All Saints' Day, The Baptism of Our Lord (the Sunday after the Epiphany), and Easter Eve (a Saturday evening service). In addition, baptism usually takes place once during the summer months. Through either the pouring on of water, or immersion in water, we are cleansed of our sins, incorporated into the Body of Christ, and called to ministry in the Name of Jesus.

body_text:
Confirmation
For more information about any of our life celebrations or to set up an appointment with someone on our church staff, call the office at 703-670-0093, or
email us
.
We encourage every person who wishes to join All Saints' Church to do so by affirming his or her faith in Jesus Christ in worship on the Sunday our Bishop visits. This is done in one of three ways, all of which include the Laying-on-of-Hands and prayer by the Bishop:
Confirmation
is for those who have never before made a mature, public affirmation of faith in Christ.
Reception
is for those who are being received into a Church of the Anglican Communion, having previously made a mature, public affirmation of faith in Christ in another denomination.
Reaffirmation
of Baptismal Vows is for those who have previously been Confirmed in or Received into a Church of the Anglican Communion and would like to reaffirm their faith in Jesus Christ.
We make our profession of faith before the Bishop, who symbolizes the fact that, as Christians, we are part of God's universal church, and not only All Saints' Church.
Read more from the Anglican Church North America
about confirmation
. (PDF)
Those Interested in Confirmation, Reaffirmation or Reception
Preparations for the Bishop's visit are made at our 7-week confirmation course,
Learning & Confirming What We Believe
, whose completion is required for Confirmation, Reception and Reaffirmation. (Those wishing to Reaffirm their Baptismal Vows who have previously been Confirmed or Received into the Anglican Church are not required to take the Confirmation Course but are strongly encouraged to.) You will need to
register
for Confirmation, Reception or Reaffirmation as well as the Confirmation Course.

body_text:
Hello, I am Sarah-Joy Reichert, a patriot in Troop VA 0428. You are invited to attend a
“Life-Saving Skills Workshop: Hands-Only CPR, Heimlich Maneuver, and Disaster Relief Hygiene Kits.”
This is for my
Stars & Stripes
project.
I will host three workshops, two in-person and with a service opportunity. A third will be virtual to learn Heimlech & hands-only CPR. Workshop #1 is on Sept. 21, 10 a.m.
During each workshop, you will have the opportunity to:
Learn hands-only CPR from a Red Cross-certified instructor
Learn abdominal thrusts (the Heimlich)
Make
Disaster Relief Hygiene Kits & Flood Buckets
to donate to The Anglican Relief and Development Fund (
ARDF
)
National Day of Service
The timing is perfect because this year AHG's National Day of Service (NDS) is "Seeing and Meeting Needs." The NDS theme calls us to serve "others in a sacrificial way that requires stepping out of your comfort zone and putting others’ interests before yours.” In particular, we are called to see a need, such as an emergency or crisis, and respond.
Why should I learn these techniques??
This past spring at an AHG event for patriots my friend was choking and indicated the universal sign of choking. I was able to perform the Heimlich helping her to dislodge what was in her throat.
According to the Red Cross, patients receiving standard and Hands-Only CPR were two times more likely to survive 30 days, compared with patients who received no CPR.
ARDF
The
Anglican Relief and Development Fund
supports local churches serving their communities after a crisis. They commit resources and connect volunteers to training and opportunities to serve. The hygiene kits would be stored by ARDF and used during a natural disaster or other crises.
RSVP
If you want to attend, sign up
here
to reserve your space at either of the events.
Donate Supplies
You can donate the items needed to make the relief kits. Details
here
. If you need to ship them, please send them to the church c/o my name. Sarah-Joy Reichert, 1485

page_title: How All Saints’ built its current home on Gideon Drive
body_text:
A vision fulfilled
All Saints’ arrived at its current Gideon Drive location through the power of prayer, God’s provision and God’s timing. It’s a testament to God’s ability to do the unimaginable in a way that defies human reason.
The story occurs in three stages, starting with John Guernsey, All Saints’ rector at the time.
During a week-long Restoring the Foundations retreat in early March, 2001, John sought inner healing for an ungodly belief. He knew All Saints’ had outgrown its building on Saratoga Lane in Woodbridge. But he struggled to believe he could lead a larger congregation at a new building.
The retreat helped John address that stronghold and paved the way toward something bigger.. Upon returning home, John took most of the following week off to pray through his RTF experience.
It was during this time that the Lord unfolded a vision to him in great detail. He shared it first with the vestry, many of whom burst into tears. Then he shared it with the staff and the same reaction occurred.
The following Sunday (March 19), he presented the vision to the congregation; the response was an immediate, "Well, of course, this is what God wants for us.”
From there, everything fell into place in just under two months.
First, All Saints’ needed to find land to build the new church on. Through prayer and fasting, the vestry sought God’s guidance. The church also contacted Bill Burke, a realtor with Long and Foster.
Bill, who was recommended by All Saints’ bishop based on his experience working with churches, began looking for possible sites. But, with few exceptions, nothing was available. The Gideon Drive property was considered, but Bill was told it was under contract.
At this point, God clearly intervened and the third part of this story occurs.
Shelby Boldt, the executive director then of Hylton Chapel, told the owner of the Gideon Drive property that All Saints’ was looking for land. On April 25, 2001, the owner’s realtor called John and expressed interest in sell
